title: Charge and the electric car
target: Explain charge interactions and trace an electric car’s energy transfers.
criteria: Predict attraction or repulsion from charge signs.
Trace energy from a battery to moving wheels.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Two small charged beads hang on insulating threads. Both beads have negative net charge. Which force direction is expected?
options: Each is pushed away from the other.
Neither feels a force because both are negative.
Only the heavier bead feels a force.
Each is pulled toward the other.
cpa.guide: Like charges repel. Each bead feels the interaction force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A positive bead is to the left of a negative bead. Which pair of electric forces is correct?
options: Both forces: right.
Positive bead: right; negative bead: left.
Both forces: left.
Positive bead: left; negative bead: right.
cpa.guide: Opposite charges attract; the forces point toward one another.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A motor runs for a while. Which statement distinguishes charge from energy?
options: Energy and charge are two names for the same quantity.
The wire creates a new supply of charge each second.
Charge circulates through the circuit while energy is transferred to motion and heating.
Charge is used up inside the motor.
cpa.guide: Circuit charge is conserved; the battery transfers energy to the load.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A battery transfers 18 J while 3 C passes. Which statement uses the units correctly?
options: 18 J describes energy; 3 C describes charge.
Both numbers describe electric force.
18 J is current; 3 C is power.
Both numbers describe mass.
cpa.guide: Joules measure energy and coulombs measure charge.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A battery-driven fan starts from rest. Which energy sequence explains its useful output?
options: Current → creation of energy from nothing.
Blade rotation → new charge → battery chemical energy only.
Chemical energy → electric charge being destroyed.
Chemical energy → electrical transfer → blade rotation.
cpa.guide: A battery supplies energy through the circuit and the motor produces mechanical rotation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A toy winch lifts a load using a battery and motor. Which account is consistent with conservation?
options: All battery energy disappears when the load stops.
Battery energy becomes increased gravitational energy plus thermal and other outputs.
The motor creates more energy than the battery supplies.
No energy transfers because circuit charge is conserved.
cpa.guide: Charge conservation does not prevent energy transfer. Include useful and less useful outputs.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
